{{Quote|Holding her is dangerous. If word of this gets out, it could generate sympathy for the Rebellion in the Senate.|Daine Jir, to Darth Vader, referring to Leia Organa|<ref name="anh" />}}
'''Daine Jir''' was a bold and outspoken [[Human/Legends|Human]] [[Gender/Legends|male]] who served as an [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Imperial]] [[Stormtrooper/Legends|stormtrooper]] officer of the [[501st Legion/Legends|501st Legion]] under [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Darth Vader]] aboard the [[Imperial I-class Star Destroyer/Legends|''Imperial I''-class Star Destroyer]] [[Devastator/Legends|''Devastator'']]. He served as a [[Commander/Legends|commander]] during the hunt for the stolen [[DS-1 Orbital Battle Station/Legends|Death Star]] [[Death Star plans/Legends|plans]] in [[0 BBY/Legends|0 BBY]]. Jir&mdash;part of a [[Jir family|family]] that had donated a genetic template for the Imperial stormtrooper development program&mdash; proved himself to be a competent and ruthless officer. However, many suspected he would not last long under Vader's command after he called one of the [[Dark Lord of the Sith/Legends|Dark Lord's]] decisions into doubt. Vader instead was impressed with Jir's brutal honesty, and promoted the officer instead of [[Telekinesis/Legends|killing]] him.

In 0 BBY, Jir led a contingent of the 501st in an [[Battle of Tatooine (Galactic Civil War)|attack]] on the [[CR90 corvette/Legends|CR90 corvette]] [[Tantive IV/Legends|''Tantive IV'']], on which Vader believed [[Senator/Legends|Senator]] [[Leia Organa Solo/Legends|Leia Organa]] had received transmissions containing the [[Death Star/Legends|Death Star]] plans. The 501st picked off the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel]] forces aboard the [[Starship/Legends|ship]] and captured Organa, but despite a thorough search of the corvette no trace of the plans could be found. After the battle, Jir was tasked with sending a distress signal from the [[Starship/Legends|ship]] and alerting the [[Imperial Senate/Legends|Imperial Senate]] that all aboard were [[Death/Legends|killed]]. His ultimate fate was unknown.

==Biography==
===Commander of the 501st===
{{Quote|&hellip;dead man walking&hellip;|Murmurs about Daine Jir after he defied Vader for the first time|<ref name="tef" />}}
[[File:Devastator-ANH.png|thumb||left|300px|Daine Jir was posted to the Imperial Star Destroyer ''Devastator''.]]
A tall, slim [[Human/Legends|Human]]<ref name="novelisation" /> [[Gender/Legends|male]],<ref name="tef" /> Daine Jir was a member of the [[Jir family]], who were known to have donated a genetic template for the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Imperial]] [[Stormtrooper/Legends|stormtrooper]] development program.<ref name="VG" /> Jir himself<ref name="tef" /> was a stormtrooper in the [[501st Legion/Legends|501st Legion]], having served as a noncombat officer<ref name="cswe">{{CSWECite|II|172|Jir, Commander Daine}}</ref> with the rank of [[Lieutenant/Legends|lieutenant]] in the same legion,<ref name="tef" /> known for its [[501st Journal|exploits]] at [[Kamino/Legends|Kamino]] and [[Polis Massa/Legends|Polis Massa]] as well as [[Death Star Uprising|quelling]] a [[Prison/Legends|prison]] break on the [[DS-1 Orbital Battle Station/Legends|Death Star]].<ref name="bf2">''[[Star Wars: Battlefront II]]''</ref> Jir subjected his [[Troop/Legends|troops]] to constant crisis simulations,<ref name="btm">''[[Star Wars: Behind the Magic]]''</ref> and those were used along with constant training regimens to ensure that he maintained high performance levels.<ref name="swe">''[[Star Wars Encyclopedia]]''</ref>

By [[0 BBY/Legends|0 BBY]], Jir and the 501st were posted aboard<ref name="swe" /> the [[Imperial I-class Star Destroyer/Legends|''Imperial I''-class Star Destroyer]]<ref name="v:tug">''[[Vader: The Ultimate Guide]]''</ref> [[Devastator/Legends|''Devastator'']], and served directly under [[Dark Lord of the Sith/Legends|Dark Lord of the Sith]] [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Darth Vader]], [[Galactic Emperor/Legends|Emperor]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine's]] enforcer.<ref name="anh" /> Vader was a fearsome figure who was known to execute his subordinates for the merest of errors,<ref name="esb">{{Film|V}}</ref> and after Jir first spoke out against one of Vader's suggestions, his peers began to count his days amongst the living; Vader had [[Telekinesis/Legends|Force choked]] men for far less. The Dark Lord, however, found Jir's brutal honesty a refreshing contrast to the usual manipulative rhetoric of most Imperial officers, and promoted him to [[Commander/Legends|commander]]. Of the officers in the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]], it was later said that Jir, like [[Admiral/Legends|Admiral]] [[Firmus Piett/Legends|Firmus Piett]] and [[Captain/Legends|Captain]] [[Janus Bonn]], was one of the select few Imperial officers who had ever earned Vader's respect.<ref name="tef" />

===Attack on the ''Tantive IV''===
In 0 BBY, members of the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Alliance to Restore the Republic]] on the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Toprawa/Legends|Toprawa]] [[Battle of Toprawa|stole plans]] to the Empire's secret Death Star project, which were transmitted to [[Senator/Legends|Imperial Senator]] [[Leia Organa Solo/Legends|Leia Organa]]&mdash;herself a member of the Rebel Alliance&mdash;and her crew on board the [[CR90 corvette/Legends|CR90 corvette]] [[Tantive IV/Legends|''Tantive IV'']]. By the time [[Imperial Intelligence/Legends|Imperial Intelligence]] located the leak, Organa had fled in the ''Tantive IV''. Vowing to retrieve the stolen information at any cost, Darth Vader took the ''Devastator'' in pursuit,<ref name="nec">''[[The New Essential Chronology]]''</ref> along with Jir and the 501st.<ref name="anh" /> Vader also hoped capturing the ship would provide the Empire with the location of the Rebels' [[Great Temple/Legends|secret base]].<ref name="nec" />

[[File:VaderPoint-ANH.png|thumb|right|230px|Jir, beside Darth Vader as he confronts Leia Organa]]
The ''Devastator'' [[Battle of Tatooine (Galactic Civil War)|intercepted]] the ''Tantive IV'' over the remote [[Planet/Legends|world]] of [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]] in the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]]; the [[Star Destroyer/Legends|Star Destroyer]] [[Tractor beam/Legends|tractor beamed]] the ship, and Vader ordered the 501st to prepare to board. Jir stayed behind with Vader as the [[Legion/Legends|legion's]] contingent of stormtroopers entered the ''Tantive IV'' to engage what few soldiers the Rebellion had defending the ship. The Imperials killed many of them, allowing Vader to enter and oversee the search for the Death Star plans. However, no trace of the plans could be found, and the Imperials were also unable to locate [[Princess/Legends|Princess]] Leia Organa.<ref name="anh" /> 

Troopers located the ''Tantive IV''{{'s}} [[Captain/Legends|captain]], [[Raymus Antilles/Legends|Raymus Antilles]]. They brought Antilles<ref name="Black Knight">{{SWRadio|Black Knight, White Princess, and Pawns}}</ref> to a spot where other captive officers were being held,<ref name="novelisation" /> where they awaited Lord Vader. Vader soon arrived. He lifted Captain Antilles by the throat and demanded to know where he had hid the Death Star plans and the Princess. When Antilles refused to answer, Vader [[Death/Legends|killed]] him and tossed his body aside.<ref name="anh" />

===Questioning the Dark Lord===
{{Quote|Send a distress signal and then inform the Senate that all aboard were killed.|Darth Vader, to Daine Jir|<ref name="anh" />}}
Before long, Organa was located, but the troops still were unable to find the Death Star plans. The stormtroopers escorted the princess to Jir and Vader, who began questioning her. Organa was defiant, reiterating that she was on a diplomatic mission and that the Senate would not stand for Vader's actions. Furious, Vader accused her of conspiring with the Rebellion and had her taken aboard his Star Destroyer for interrogation at a later time.<ref name="anh" /> After she was gone, Jir spoke to Vader. He argued that Organa would not buckle under even Vader's interrogation. He bluntly told Vader that holding her in custody could generate sympathy for the Rebel Alliance in the Senate<ref name="anh" /> and that killing her would be wiser.<ref name="novelisation" /> The Dark Lord, however, was adamant that he needed her in custody because she was his only link to the Rebel base,<ref name="anh" /> though he confessed to having no idea why she had come to Tatooine. Jir confirmed that the ''Devastator''{{'s}} [[Sensor/Legends|sensors]] had found no sign of a military presence in the system.<ref name="Black Knight" /> Commander Jir, betraying a bit of sympathy for the princess,<ref name="novelisation" /> then warned the Dark Lord that Organa would rather die than give away any information to Vader.<ref name="anh" /> 

Vader acknowledged Jir's warnings but was undeterred. He ordered the commander to send a false distress signal from the ship and inform the Senate that all aboard were killed.<ref name="anh" /> Jir's official explanation was that the ''Tantive IV'' had been destroyed in an [[Asteroid/Legends|asteroid]] storm, with no survivors.<ref name="DB">{{DB|starship|tantiveiv|Rebel blockade runners}}</ref> After that, Vader ordered Jir to have the Alderaanian ship vaporized so that no evidence would be left of the attack.<ref name="novelisation" /> 

The ''Devastator'' left the [[Tatoo system/Legends|Tatoo system]] and headed for the Death Star. Organa was transferred to [[Detention Block AA-23/Legends|Detention Block AA-23]], where Vader subjected her to a [[Torture/Legends|brutal interrogation]].<ref name="anh" /> There, Jir's prediction proved true: Organa refused to betray the Alliance; she did not reveal the location either of the Death Star plans or of the Rebel base.<ref name="dst">{{SWRadio|Death Star's Transit}}</ref> Jir's fate after the Battle of Tatooine remained unknown.<ref name="btm" />

==Personality and traits==
{{Quote|She'll die before she'll tell you anything.''"<br />"''Leave that to me.|Daine Jir and Darth Vader|<ref name="anh" />}}
[[File:Jir_Vader.png|thumb|left|265px|Commander Jir alongside Darth Vader]]
A typical Imperial leader,<ref name="CCG">{{CCG|set=A New Hope Limited|cardname=Imperial Commander}}</ref> Daine Jir was bold and outspoken,<ref name="tef" /> with [[Color/Legends|brown]] hair and light skin.<ref name="anh" /> Competent and ruthless,<ref name="tef" /> his aggressive and independent thinking made him respected, even by Lord Vader.<ref name="TPS">{{Topps|set=2013 Topps Star Wars Galactic Files Series 2|cardname=Daine Jir}}</ref> He was known to question the decisions of Darth Vader without fear of the consequences,<ref name="tef" /> being one of the few Imperial officers not afraid of the Dark Lord.<ref name="btm" /> While other officers believed Jir would be soon executed, his suggestions were appreciated by Vader, who personally promoted him from lieutenant to commander.<ref name="cswe" />

==Behind the scenes==
{{Quote|She should be destroyed, Lord Vader.|Jir, to Darth Vader, in the Marvel comic ''Star Wars 1''|<ref name="MSW1">[[Star Wars (1977) 1|''Star Wars'' (1977) 1]]</ref>}}
Daine Jir's character has appeared in numerous adaptations across different media, introducing many small differences and inconsistencies. The character first appeared in the [[1976]] [[Star Wars: A New Hope (novelization)|novelization]] of [[Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope|''Star Wars'': Episode IV ''A New Hope'']], where he is not given a name but is described as "a tall, slim soldier wearing the sign of an Imperial Commander." He questions Vader's decision to hold Princess Leia and recommends instead that she "be destroyed immediately." After their discussion, Vader gives the commander two orders: to send a fake distress signal and oversee the search for the Death Star plans.<ref name="novelisation" />

In [[1977]], Jir appeared in ''A New Hope''.<ref name="anh" /> His scenes were filmed in mid-[[1976]] in [[Elstree Studios]].<ref name="TMOSW">''[[The Making of Star Wars: The Definitive Story Behind the Original Film]]''</ref> The identity of the actor who played him was not known for many years, but in [[2007]], ''[[The Making of Star Wars: The Definitive Story Behind the Original Film]]'' included a photograph caption stating that the "commander" in scene 11 was played by Constantin De Goguel.<ref name="TMOSW" /> However, less than a month later, the [[StarWars.com]] [[Visual Guides]] authored by [[Pablo Hidalgo]] stated that Jir was portrayed by [[Al Lampert]], as per the film's production notes.<ref name="VG" /> Lampert himself related in a [[2011]] interview that Jir was to be portrayed by Scottish actor [[Ken Hutchison]], but he had a beard which [[George Lucas]] disapproved of, and the role was given to Lampert.<ref name="Aficionado">{{Blogspot|subdomain=starwarsaficionado|url=2011/09/al-lampert-remembers-star-wars.html|name=Star Wars Aficionado|text=Al Lampert Remembers "Star Wars"|date=2011-09-24}}</ref> In the film, the character is still unnamed. His dialogue is somewhat shorter than in the novelization. Vader orders him to send the fake distress call, but he directs his order to search for the Death Star plans to another officer, Nahdonnis Praji.<ref name="anh" /> 

[[File:DaineJir-Marvel.png|thumb|right|150px|Jir in the Marvel adaptation of ''A New Hope'']]
Jir also appears in the [[1977]] [[Star Wars (1977) 1|first issue]] of [[Marvel Comics|Marvel]]'s ''A New Hope'' adaptation, though with a different appearance sporting black sideburns. His dialogue is shortened to just one line, urging Vader to destroy the princess&mdash; a line in the novelization but not the film. Also like the novel, Vader orders Jir rather than Praji to lead the search on Tatooine's surface.<ref name="MSW1" /> 

In the [[Star Wars (radio)|''Star Wars'' radio dramatization]], aired in [[1981]], there are times when a voice actor is heard as an Imperial commander within the [[Black Knight, White Princess, and Pawns|third episode]]. First, the voice actor is heard hailing the ''Tantive IV'' near Toprawa and then Tatooine, ordering the Rebel ship to surrender.<ref name="Black Knight" /> This was established to be Commander Praji, in the 2007 novel ''[[The Rise and Fall of Darth Vader]]''.<ref name="rise">''[[The Rise and Fall of Darth Vader]]''</ref> Second, the voice actor is heard as a commander who captures and beats Captain Antilles before Vader comes aboard; this version has Vader boarding the ''Tantive'' somewhat later than in the film. Finally, the actor is heard as Jir, as he argues with Vader in a scene adapted from the film with some additional dialogue in which he and Vader wonder aloud why the Princess has come to Tatooine.<ref name="Black Knight" /> Given the voice actor's confirmation in portraying both Jir and Praji in the episode, it is unclear if it is Jir, Praji, or a separate character who captures and beats Antilles.

In [[1997]], [[Decipher]]'s [[Star Wars Customizable Card Game|''Star Wars'' Customizable Card Game]] first gave the character a name, identifying him as Commander Daine Jir in a card in the ''[[A New Hope Limited]]'' expansion. "Daine Jir" is likely a play on the word "danger," inspired by Jir's line: "Holding her is dangerous."<ref name="tef" /> In [[2003]], the [[Star Wars Trading Card Game|''Star Wars'' Trading Card Game]] identified Jir as a "Star Destroyer Commander" in the [[Imperial Navy/Legends|Imperial Navy]],<ref name="TCG">{{TCG|set=Battle of Yavin|link=https://swtcg.com/Content/Images/Cards/ANH/Star_Destroyer_Commander.webp?v=2|cardname=Star Destroyer Commander}}</ref> which contradicts the novelization, which describes him as a commander of Stormtroopers.<ref name="tef" />

In 2007, an article in [[Star Wars Insider 96|''Star Wars Insider'' 96]] called "[[The Empire's Finest: Who's Who in the Imperial Military|The Empire's Finest]]" told Daine Jir's backstory, for the first time revealing something of the commander's life before he found himself next to Darth Vader on the deck of the ''Tantive IV.'' It confirmed that he was an officer of the 501st Stormtrooper Legion.<ref name="tef" />
